Subject: Partnership - distribution + lead registration (initial term sheet attached)

Diego / Marissa,

Great to connect last week. As discussed, Stratum Analytics is ready to pilot a reseller distribution path for our integration with Redwood — we help embed Redwood inference in our vertical analytics product and can surface it to ~120 enterprise customers.

High-level asks from our side:
- A tiered revenue-share that starts at 15% for referral-only and scales up to 30% for full reseller where Stratum invoices customers.
- Lead registration protection for 12 months for registered leads (we'll provide lead evidence and contact+activity logs).
- A short-term onboarding rebate (one-time) to offset integration certification costs for our engineering team.

I've attached a draft rebate schedule and a simple Lead Registration spreadsheet showing historic monthly lead volumes. Can we set a 30-minute call this week to align on where Redwood typically draws the line between referral vs reseller economics?

Attachments: Stratum_Rebate_Sched_v1.pdf (PDF), Stratum_Lead_Sample.csv (CSV)

Thanks,

Ariel — thanks for the note and the materials, much appreciated.

Quick responses:
- We can support both referral and reseller models, but economics differ (referral = finders fee, reseller = revenue share + contractual reseller obligations). Redwood's standard lead registration window is 6 months; 12 months is not unheard of for integration partners but we need tighter evidence requirements (activity logs, signed contacts).
- On rebates: we typically do a one-time integration credit tied to a technical certification milestone rather than a pure cash rebate. That helps align onboarding delivery.

Can we do Wed 7/8 11:00 PT? If that works I'll loop in Legal/Channel Ops. Also copied Ben to flag larger commercial exceptions (enterprise deal threshold) early.

Diego Fernandez

Subject: Proposed channel economics + lead routing (draft)

Team / Ariel — following our call, attached is a working draft for channel economics and a proposed lead routing matrix. Key bullets:

- Commission tiers (net revenue to Redwood):
  * Referral (Redwood invoices): 15% for ARR < $50k, 18% for ARR $50k-$150k, 20% for ARR > $150k.
  * Reseller (partner invoices): 25% flat on billed revenue; 30% for transacted deals where Stratum also provides first-year managed services.
- Onboarding credit: one-time credit equal to 2 months of expected run-rate (applies only when partner completes integration certification and a joint go-to-market plan).
- Lead registration: 9-month protection for registered leads with mandatory lead intake form + evidence package (first touch, qualified contact, and pipeline activity).
- Exclusivity: not supported; however we offer a 90-day lead-first exclusivity window for newly registered, pipeline-verified enterprise opportunities (subject to validation).
- Payment terms: Net 45 for rebate/commission payouts; invoice cadence quarterly.

Open items we need legal to confirm: audit access to deal evidence, timing of payment triggers, and whether the onboarding credit should be converted to a marketing co-op for tax/sales ops simplicity.

Attachments: MAP-and-Lead-Registration.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks — Marissa Cole
Channel Operations Lead | Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — quick piece of commercial feedback from the sales side:

- If Stratum will be driving enterprise introductions, we should consider an accelerated upfront rebate for deals > $150k ARR to help close procurement timing (one-time 10% onboarding credit applied against first invoice). That reduces friction for large customers and gives Stratum cash to help with procurement resources.
- Also propose changing commission payout on reseller to Net 30 for the first two quarters of the program while we validate volumes; after Q2 we can move to Net 45 as proposed.

Laura — looping you for alliance perspective on whether 9-month lead protection is defensible operationally (audit load / false claim risk).
